meaning.what_it_means: The low-response zones are open fractures. Storage in the 120-250 m window is the largest of the three readings (P50 10,805 m3) and a pathway from the upper zone reaches the well in 97-100 % of realisations across the candidate sites.
meaning.what_to_do: Drill the priority site (A) first; log fractures and water strikes between 100 and 300 m; keep the recharge package because the demand still draws the aquifer down: S6 drawdown P50 1.5 m with an open boundary (low (< 5 m)) and 2.9 m with a closed boundary (low (< 5 m)).
meaning.boundary_effect: Open boundary: drawdown P50 1.5 m, recharge retained 1 %. Closed boundary: drawdown P50 2.9 m, recharge retained 100 %. With a closed boundary the site lives on its own recharge, so the recharge package matters more.
meaning.borehole_evidence_that_confirms_it: open fractures with water strikes in at least two of the predicted intervals (P2); yield step test holds

meaning.what_it_means: Only the strongest low-response class (C1) is fractured. Fractures are patchy: storage P50 6,296 m3 and a pathway from the upper zone in 20-34 % of realisations - a borewell may hit a fracture or miss it.
meaning.what_to_do: Drill to the logged fracture, not to a fixed depth; keep the reserve site ready; S6 drawdown P50 1.7 m with an open boundary (low (< 5 m)) and 3.1 m with a closed boundary (low (< 5 m)); recharge must be placed where the borehole proves a connected fracture.
meaning.boundary_effect: Open boundary: drawdown P50 1.7 m, recharge retained 1 %. Closed boundary: drawdown P50 3.1 m, recharge retained 100 %. With a closed boundary the site lives on its own recharge, so the recharge package matters more.
meaning.borehole_evidence_that_confirms_it: one fractured interval near the predicted depth; other low-response intervals dry or tight

meaning.what_it_means: No ADMT class carries water; C1 is clay/gouge. Storage is the smallest (P50 4,806 m3) and the site depends on weathered-zone water and on recharge.
meaning.what_to_do: Reduce the borewell demand, rely first on roof water, tanks and biopools; S6 drawdown P50 5.2 m with an open boundary (moderate (5-20 m)) and 4.7 m with a closed boundary (low (< 5 m)); a single borewell should be treated as a test well, not a supply.
meaning.boundary_effect: Open boundary: drawdown P50 5.2 m, recharge retained 1 %. Closed boundary: drawdown P50 4.7 m, recharge retained 100 %. With a closed boundary the site lives on its own recharge, so the recharge package matters more.
meaning.borehole_evidence_that_confirms_it: low-response intervals logged as clay/gouge or tight rock; no strike in 100-300 m

decisions.decision: Dry-spell checks start the roof tanks at their average content on 1 December from the daily run, not full; pure-water top-up fills A and B from treated wastewater with no use, outside the storm season; borewell top-up is not used
decisions.reason: Full tanks at the start were optimistic; borewell top-up would raise the peak pumping day

decisions.decision: Storm credit = space of chamber B kept empty (default 100 %), valid only for storms in the storm season (default Sep to Nov); the daily run shows only about 63 % of tank space free on days of 64.5 mm or more, so 50 % is the careful value until the rule is proven in operation
decisions.reason: A chamber that is full when a storm starts gives no relief; outside the season there is no credit

decisions.decision: Each flat building has three roof chambers: A pure water (reserve, filled first, used last), B swing (used first, kept for storms in the storm season), flush chamber 6 x 5 x 4 m (108 m3 usable, about 10 days, no effect on the balance). Amenity tank 648 m3 stays separate
decisions.reason: One chamber can be emptied for a sudden event while the reserve stays full; sizes are proposals until the structural and plumbing design

decisions.decision: The Net zero storm check takes no credit for roof tank space by default (0 % kept empty); credit only through a typed share, because a tank full when the storm starts gives no relief; the daily run shows tanks 81 % empty on average at the start of heavy-rain days
decisions.reason: Prevents the reservoir size resting on a tank level that is not controlled; a storm-buffer share needs a level rule or overflow arrangement in the design

decisions.decision: Roof tank design carried into the model (v1.17.6): underground tank per flat building 648 m3 usable (30-day basis; built as two chambers of 6 x 15 x 4 m, 720 m3), amenity tank 648 m3, set as separate inputs in the Net zero plan view and read by the Net zero storm check, the Risk calendar and drought view and the Closed loop view
decisions.reason: Hydrogeologist confirmed the 2 x (6 x 15 x 4 m) tank for each flat building; tank volumes and the 7,680 / 5,940 m2 roof split are design proposals, not yet drawn

decisions.decision: Two grades (pure water for the flats; concentrate and treated wastewater for flushing and irrigation) is the default supply grade in the studio; one grade stays as a switch
decisions.reason: One grade makes 10,266 m3/yr of concentrate that needs a 10,266 m2 pond (23.6 % of the lease), which the lease cannot give; two grades needs 7,372 m3/yr pumped, 2 borewells and no pond. MD to confirm

decisions.decision: Reverse osmosis concentrate is used in toilet flushing only (and in irrigation only up to a share set by the planner, default 0 %); fresh-water plants and trees and the fountain get no concentrate
decisions.reason: Concentrate carries about four times the salt of the feed; the lease has fresh-water plants and trees. Flushing needs 11,588 m3/yr against 5,056 m3/yr of concentrate, so keeping irrigation clear costs nothing; salinity and sodium tests and salt-tolerant flushing pipes are still needed

decisions.decision: Plan for a 130-day dry spell (1 year in 10) and check against 178 days (longest on record); the Closed loop view shows the days stored rain and the treated tank last and what the borewells must pump and how low their yield can fall
decisions.reason: The yearly totals hide the daily capacity needed in a long dry spell; the design basis for borewell capacity and pumping tests should be stated

decisions.decision: Dry spells are reported over the whole year (a spell is followed across 31 December), with the three rainy-season windows kept as secondary rows
decisions.reason: The three windows (Jun-Nov, Jun-Sep, Oct-Dec) left out the dry season, so the table showed a longest spell of 61 days where the record has 178; storage is sized by the whole-year spell

decisions.decision: Aquifer draft is compared with all the water the lease puts back (open-ground soak-in plus recharge wells) and reported as a net draw; the unlinked parts between the Net Zero, Drought and Closed loop views are stated on the screen (pond land not removed from the lease; storm water use typed by hand)
decisions.reason: The 8.5 times figure ignored the recharge wells and was described as if it included them; readers need to know where the three views share inputs and where they do not

decisions.decision: Every figure on the Closed loop screen and in the final report is labelled: per year or per day, average / dry / peak, before or after reverse osmosis; demand is shown as 96 (wet months), 109 (average) and 135 (dry day) m3/d, and pumping by month
decisions.reason: Readers took the 109 m3/d average, the 122 m3/d January demand, the 16,812 pumped and the 12,609 borewell pure water for contradictions; they are different cuts of the same water

decisions.decision: The three-stage plan (borewells only, add wastewater reuse, add rain reuse) is part of the model (v1.17.0), with borewells needed on the peak day and the concentrate pond area (concentrate / net evaporation, placeholder 1,000 mm a year)
decisions.reason: The final water demand and supply report quoted stage figures, the number of borewells and a pond size that had been worked outside the app; they now come from the model so the report and the model agree and change together when yield, hours or evaporation are measured

decisions.decision: All water used on the lease must be high quality (v1.16.0): every use (flats, flushing, fountain, irrigation) takes rain treated by ultrafiltration and UV, pure water from the wastewater membranes, or borewell water through reverse osmosis; no lower-grade use, so all concentrate has no use and must be kept on the lease. Borewell supply set temporarily from regional deep-borewell reports (user screenshot): 3 borewells x 3.6 m3/h (about 1 L/s) x 12 h/d = 129.6 m3/d; placeholders until the first test pumping and water test
decisions.reason: Hydrogeologist's instruction: no low-grade water; deep (Aquifer II) water in Malur Taluk often has fluoride and nitrate above limits; the block is over-exploited (stage about 179 to 180 %)

decisions.decision: The Studio AI assistant is given the Storm & Storage Plan (v1.15.1): a project vocabulary rule (net zero = net zero discharge of storm water, not carbon), a STORM & STORAGE PLAN context block on the Run & scenarios step (storm register, GEV design storms, method notes) and a digest of the results on screen (net zero rows, clearing days, levers, risk calendar, level rules, closed loop)
decisions.reason: The assistant answered a question on the Net Zero Plan with carbon and energy advice because the step had no storm context and no definition of the term. The digest comes from the page, so it matches the user's current inputs; results must be calculated on the tab first.

decisions.decision: Recharge well contact area from geometry and tier (shaft/pit in saprolite; borewells cased above and open over their own tier) instead of one 40 m2; Darcy K x A x i stays the default; the injection-well (Thiem) rule is an option for borewells
decisions.reason: The hydrogeologist pointed out that the contact area changes with the depth of the recharge well. Defaults (shaft 1.0 m x 15 m, borewell 0.165 m) are placeholders until the structure design; the injection rule assumes the open section is below the water table. Field test: injection or falling-head test at RZ-13.

decisions.decision: Default reservoir raised from 4,800 to 5,000 m3 (about 1,670 m2 of water at 3 m, 3.8 % of the lease)
decisions.reason: The reservoir is sized on the volume of the 135 mm GEV 100-year day on wet ground; as a 1 h cloudburst the same day needs about 4,900 m3 because the wells cannot work during it. Drains and inlets are a separate design (short-duration intensity, IMD 1/3 rule, about 61 mm/h over 40 min, about 0.6 m3/s for the lease) - not yet in Studio.

decisions.decision: Design storms from the GEV distribution (L-moments) instead of Gumbel in all Storm & storage views (v1.14.0): 100-year 1-day rain 135 mm (was 125 mm); default reservoir 4,800 m3 (holds 135 mm on wet ground, 4,776 m3 needed); Gumbel shown for comparison only
decisions.reason: The three largest days (148.6 mm 1981, 142.9 mm 2021, 137.0 mm 1991) lie well above the Gumbel line; Gumbel rejected (likelihood ratio p = 0.03), GEV shape 0.13 (heavier tail). Uncertainty is wide (100-year 110-162 mm, 90 % bootstrap); the daily 0.25 deg grid understates point rain.
decisions.by: Hydrogeologist (asked to switch to GEV), Claude

decisions.decision: Storm & storage plan audit fixes (v1.13.1): detail views aligned with the net zero inputs (100 % capture, road from width x length, 4,400 m3 buffer, 63.5 m3/d use for 141 flats); 212 mm run as a 72 h three-day storm without a 1-day return period; roof wetting loss stated (none for sizing, 1 mm per rain day for supply); one evaporation rule; empty-months note for the level rule
decisions.reason: Audit on 3 Nov 2026 found the detail views on old placeholders, a 3-day total treated as a 1-day storm, and unstated differences between views. The strict rule keeping the reservoir empty in Sep-Nov remains an open decision.

decisions.decision: Closed loop with NEWater-type treatment (ultrafiltration, reverse osmosis, UV) added to the model (v1.13.0) with borewells as a back-up source. At 5 persons per flat, 2,000 m3 treated-water tank, 75 % recovery, borewell and outside water needed falls from about 15,800 to about 7,700 m3 a year (dry-10 % year 10,000; driest 12,800); with an 85 % treated share, half the planted area and 20 % lower use it falls to about 1,500. Using pure water for drinking changes the need by under 1 %, so drinking use is a provision, not a necessity. A roof tank of 5,000 m3 and a draw-down capacity of about 580 m3/d remain the main protection beyond the 125 mm storm.
decisions.reason: Hydrogeologist asked that NEWater be considered for all uses to close the loop and meet the water demand, and asked whether borewells had been considered. Borewell yield, recovery, drinking share and recharge share are placeholders; draft is about 3.9 times the recharge assumed on the open ground, so aquifer sustainability must be checked (test pumping at RZ-13, CGWB block category). Direct drinking use of reclaimed water has no settled approval route in India.
decisions.status: suggested; to be approved by the hydrogeologist

decisions.decision: Risk calendar and drought view added (v1.12.0): monthly free-space rule (strict: largest day on record per month, moderate: 1-in-10-year month) and a 125-year daily water balance for 141 flats at 135 lpcd, 4-6 persons per flat (5 central). Outside water is needed every year for drinking-quality use (about 15,700 m3/yr at 5 persons, no roof tank, 117 m3/d wells); roof tanks up to about 5,000 m3 remove the spill years, more adds little.
decisions.reason: Hydrogeologist asked for the risk calendar and drought planning using the flats, fountain and greenery. Planted area, fountain size, evaporation, persons per flat and well yield are assumptions or untested; the outside supply is a requirement, not proof the wells can deliver it. Treated-wastewater surplus (mostly June to November) needs storage, recharge or use.
decisions.status: suggested; to be approved by the hydrogeologist

decisions.decision: Runoff coefficients corrected (roof 0.95, tar road 0.90 after 1 mm wetting; green ground by curve number 78) and the overflow basin removed from the net zero plan (v1.11.1). With the corrected coefficients the 125 mm storm on wet ground needs 4,367 m3 (default reservoir 4,400 m3, about 1,470 m2 of water at 3 m); storms above 125 mm are stress cases showing the volume beyond the reservoir.
decisions.reason: Hydrogeologist asked for the correct coefficient for every surface and said the overflow basin concept will not be considered. Roof 0.85 was low against standard tables (0.75-0.95) and the NRCS curve number 98; a higher coefficient is the safe side for sizing. Values are standard, not measured: meter a roof and the road in a storm. Main register A07 (0.85) is untouched and differs.
decisions.status: suggested; to be approved by the hydrogeologist

decisions.decision: Net zero plan made the first view of the Storm & storage plan tab (v1.11.0): all rain on the lease accounted for by surface (roof 13,620 m2, tar road 12.19 m x 300 m assumed, green and permeable ground the rest); 100 % of runoff led to a reservoir; overflow basin for storms beyond the reservoir; design storms 90 mm (operating), 125 mm (100-year Gumbel), 150-250 mm (stress, overflow basin).
decisions.reason: Hydrogeologist stated the land cover and asked that the 4,350 m3 of rain per 100 mm be fully used, with net zero discharge, and that the Gumbel range from Heavy 90 mm to Extremely heavy 250 mm be the design storms. Return periods beyond the 125-year record are extrapolations (the record day is 149 mm; 250 mm is the IMD class, not a Gumbel storm). Road length, open-ground curve number and basin infiltration are placeholders; replace with the site plan, a double-ring infiltration test and a basin-floor test.

decisions.decision: Storm sequence added to the storm planner (v1.10.1): several storms run through one buffer and one set of wells; pore-space fill of each tier shown as two bounds (no recovery; drainage with the M7d mean delay) because the saved M7d results cannot resolve recovery within days to weeks.
decisions.reason: Hydrogeologist asked whether back-to-back monsoon storms overwhelm the wells and how much space each tier regains between storms. Wetness from the previous 5-day rain follows the standard SCS limits; it is not calibrated. Example storms are placeholders until the IMD wet-spell record or forecast is typed in. Replace the drainage bound with measured injection rate and water-level recovery after the first storm.

decisions.decision: Storm response planner (M7e) added as a fast, non-MODFLOW module: event runoff (SCS-CN, roof and hard-surface coefficients), optional buffer, per-tier well intake limits and operating rules; underground fate read from saved M7d central results. Buffer is optional (a pond is only one example). All catchment, buffer and runoff values are placeholders "suggested, not yours yet" until the site plan is ready. Whole-site water balance remains deferred.
decisions.reason: Hydrogeologist asked for planning of cloudburst water capture across the recharge tiers

decisions.decision: ** Use the ADMT readings (I‑POS, I‑NEU, I‑NEG) from the Studio interface to pick the first borehole location; the open (B1) or closed (B2) boundary condition will then govern the hydrogeological response. The first drilled borehole will confirm whether the assumed 30‑80 m or 150‑250 m interval yields water, after which the team can adjust the next site accordingly.
decisions.reason: AI suggestion accepted in Studio step 0 (run SID-20261019-104700). Question: Explain what this site setting means for choosing a borewell site and depth.

decisions.decision: Optional fifth rock structure "fracture corridor" in the cloudburst tiers: one planar fracture zone through the recharge point at a 120 m reference depth; only K is raised along it (to the register high value of each layer, weighted by the share of the 40 m cell inside the zone); Sy stays at the layer value; strike, dip and width are cloudburst assumptions CB10-CB12 (suggested, not yours yet; strike is unknown from passive ADMT and is sampled 0-180 deg in uncertainty mode); off by default
decisions.reason: the zoned structures vary K only through the ADMT probability and cannot test dipping fracture zones; the other four structures are unchanged (checked: identical results on 80 shared rows)
decisions.by: Claude, at the hydrogeologist's request for assumption-based tests
decisions.status: adopted as an option; values not yet confirmed

decisions.decision: Siddanahalli: 17 recharge-zone points (RZ-1 to RZ-17) found from storability by tier in run SID-20261019-104700
decisions.reason: storability index of the M5 volume mapped for CB1 to CB4 and the readings I-POS and I-NEU, tagged with the nearest ADMT zone; candidates for recharge tests, not confirmed

decisions.decision: Recharge zone (RZ) points are a separate list from the borewell candidates A to G: found from the storability of the M5 volume in each of the four tiers (positive and neutral readings), tagged with the nearest ADMT zone, run through the same cloudburst comparison. Layers stay separate; no combined score.
decisions.reason: The user: borewell priority and reserve is one question, favourable recharge zones another, found from storability by tier and the interpreted zones

decisions.decision: Recharge locations are compared with storability, connectivity and the cloudburst simulation as separate layers, never combined into one score; every ranking shows the share of parameter sets in which a site is best, and quick screening (central case only) is labelled as direction, not certainty
decisions.reason: A site with the highest storability is not automatically the best place to recharge (delay, water held in dry rock and loss through the boundary matter), and ensemble spread must not be hidden

decisions.decision: Run reports (Word and PDF) are built by reading a finished run only; they hold the assumptions used, every scenario, and the stated status line, and never change the run
decisions.reason: Reports must show exactly what was assumed and simulated, for each run, and must not be a second place where numbers can be typed

decisions.decision: Water quality (M11) not considered for now; the deeper tier is reported as the experimental direct-recharge case (S5B gate not met)
decisions.reason: user instruction; framework gate

decisions.decision: Main cloudburst results use roof catchment only (register roof area and runoff coefficient); extra catchment and a finite buffer tank are optional switches with placeholder ranges; default buffer is 'ample'
decisions.reason: site plan not ready; results should show tier behaviour, not an unknown tank size

decisions.decision: Tiers above the water table get a simple unsaturated-zone delay (depth to water minus tier depth, divided by an assumed seepage rate) and an assumed held-back share; full UZF left for a later version
decisions.reason: register puts the water table at 30/90/200 m bgl, so shallow and medium tiers are usually above it
decisions.by: user (do what is good, explain what/why/how)

decisions.decision: Design storm for cloudburst scenarios from the IMD 0.25 deg daily record 1901-2025: 1-day depth 85 / 113 / 149 mm (Gumbel 10-yr, 50-yr, record of 11 Sep 1981)
decisions.reason: cloudburst volume must come from the local rainfall record; hourly intensity not available

decisions.decision: Cloudburst storage tiers aligned to the existing model layers: shallow = layer 1 (0-20 m), medium = layer 2 (20-60 m), medium to deep = layers 3-4 (60-175 m), deeper = layer 5 (175-250 m)
decisions.reason: avoids rebuilding the grid; keeps earlier results comparable

decisions.decision: Treat all current model output as untested scenario input. Wait for the first borehole lithology, strike, and flow data before accepting any interpretation as correct. Use the borehole to select the appropriate ADMT reading and boundary condition for future modeling.
decisions.reason: AI suggestion accepted in Studio step 2 (run SID-20261019-104700). Question: do you think all the interpretation is correct

decisions.decision: Site A (Priority 1): Drill first as an exploratory borewell; drill to at least 250 m
decisions.reason: Studio Step 4, run SID-20261019-104700: Highest zone score on site (Z01, 9) on N3, supported by crossing line E4; not at a line end; low on oblique sections S2 and S6 (100-130 m)

decisions.decision: CGWB all-India water-level PDFs used for Aquifer I (shallow) only - wells within 30 km; not used for the deep head
decisions.reason: they record dug/shallow wells

decisions.decision: D-012 revised: zoned K starts from the sampled layer K (= layered case); permeable-class share raises K toward the register high, low-K-class share (negative reading) lowers it toward the register low; other cells keep the sampled K
decisions.reason: readings then differ only in the ADMT-class cells; a "no fracture" reading can never create permeability

decisions.decision: Regional plausibility check: S0 seasonal amplitude 0.9-8.2 m and dry-season depth to water 10.25-198 m bgl (CGWB Malur 2016 Aquifer II); results reported for all runs AND for plausible runs only - implausible runs are not deleted
decisions.reason: regional analogue, not calibration

decisions.decision: Assumption register v2 created from regional evidence (E1): rainfall 623/844/1311 mm (IMD 1991-2020), monsoon share 0.66/0.76/0.87, recharge coefficient 0.01/0.03/0.10, depth to water 30/90/200 m, Sy fractured 0.0002/0.001/0.005, Sy jointed 0.0001/0.0004/0.002; v1 kept read-only
decisions.reason: IMD grid replaces CHIRPS; CGWB wells and NAQUIM Malur 2016 storage imply v1 Sy about 10x too high
decisions.by: user (use IMD grid and CGWB levels)

decisions.decision: Three readings of the ADMT classes carried in parallel: I-POS (C1-C3 permeable), I-NEU (C1 permeable), I-NEG (no permeable class; C1 = clay/gouge, low K). M5-M8, OUT and PRED report every reading; none is adopted before borehole evidence
decisions.reason: instruction "decide from all sides - positive, neutral, negative"

decisions.decision: M7a without vadose delay/UZF/clogging; M7c GWT not activated; S5B inactive
decisions.reason: V1 scope; M11 gate

decisions.decision: M7 zoned EPM: permeable-class share orders K inside the registered range (log-interpolation low->high)
decisions.reason: no K values from ADMT

decisions.decision: M7 domain 1.6 x 1.6 km, 40 m cells, 7 layers to 600 m, flat top 918 m, Newton; effects reported as differences from S0 with identical parameters
decisions.reason: no regional head data; differences cancel spin-up trends

decisions.decision: M6: within each unit the class sets the position inside the registered Sy range (HP-L upper half, HP-H lower half)
decisions.reason: no new parameter outside the register

decisions.decision: M5 soft conditioning = simple kriging of deviations from depth-dependent class shares; nugget and ranges selected by leave-one-line-out (45 settings)
decisions.reason: ordinary kriging with zero nugget failed the test (skill < 0 on all lines)

decisions.decision: Class -> HP mapping is a PROPOSAL by fixed rules (shape_z <= -0.5 -> HP-L, >= +0.5 -> HP-H); only C1 is candidate permeable
decisions.reason: needs hydrogeologist approval (framework M4)

decisions.decision: GMM k chosen by the predeclared rule (90 % of BIC improvement with seed ARI >= 0.70) -> full covariance, k = 7
decisions.reason: rule fixed before fitting; repeat-survey kappa reported for every k (all <= 0.32)

decisions.decision: D1-D5 rules declared in site_config before metrics; metrics use the DEPTH SHAPE (station static shift removed); station-level agreement reported separately as a lateral item
decisions.reason: depth classes concern depth; static shift is depth-independent

decisions.decision: No request to the vendor for the frequency table; A01 kept as nominal depth x scale factor 0.6-1.6
decisions.reason: user decision

decisions.decision: Borewell cross-check controlling version: Table_borewell_crosscheck.csv (15 Oct); report §8.5 wording superseded
decisions.reason: newer two-direction analysis

decisions.decision: Transformer influence radius 120 m; cells inside are excluded from conditioning
decisions.reason: final value from the 14-15 Oct analysis (supersedes 50 m)

decisions.decision: Master record = first record of each line; N8/E3 repeats used only for repeatability and class-stability tests
decisions.reason: keeps one acquisition per line; repeats test, not average

decisions.decision: Originals in D:\Siddanahalli are copied (never moved) to `00_raw_readonly`, with SHA-256 manifest and read-only flags
decisions.reason: framework §9
